notes:
- Fonts can be downloaded inside the app: Settings > Type & reading now lists three free families - JetBrains Mono, Inter and Roboto - and fetches one from Google Fonts when you tap Download. Nothing is packaged in the APK: only the regular and bold files are kept in the app's own storage, and a family already downloaded is applied instantly without touching the network.
- Downloaded fonts bring their real bold: The theme builds one family from the downloaded regular and 700 cuts, validates both before use and caches the result by path and file length. The resolved family is installed once in the app's MaterialTheme typography, so every screen, dialog, sheet and settings control draws with it. An imported document stays a single file and uses the platform's bold; a missing or unreadable file still falls back to the chosen system face instead of failing a screen.
- The profile banner is still: The header's artwork never settled: it faded in, jumped sideways to start an automatic sweep, and kept moving under the account's name. The sweep is gone, so a banner arrives once and stays where it is. A changed banner also resets to its own measurement instead of borrowing the previous picture's size for a frame, which was the second half of the flicker.
- Five system fonts to choose from: Settings > Type & reading now offers the five faces Android ships - Default, Sans Serif, Serif, Monospace and Cursive - instead of only the system default or an imported file. The choice is stored under its own key, so removing an imported font returns to the face you picked rather than resetting to Default. Every option is a platform family, so none can fail to render.
- Text crossfades stop re-measuring the bar: The profile title and the Library subtitle faded between two strings with the default size transform, which animated the container's measured width and moved the control beside it for the length of the fade. Both crossfades now animate alpha only, so a name arriving or a count landing changes the text and nothing around it.
- Discord sign-in now gets an access token: The Discord page could open a browser but never came back with anything: Discord gives a browser no way to hand a token to an app, so linking meant asking the reader to dig out their own token by hand. It now runs a real OAuth2 authorization-code sign-in with PKCE (S256), redirected to anisequel://discord and exchanged on the device, with the verifier never leaving it. The paste path stays underneath as the fallback for an install with no application ID.
- A Discord application ID field: An OAuth flow needs an application whose registered redirect URI is anisequel://discord, and AniSequel has never shipped one - the same situation as AniList's client ID. Settings > Discord now remembers the application ID you give it and stays disabled until it looks like a real snowflake, so a typo is a sentence under the field rather than Discord's invalid-URL page.
- OAuth tokens are sent with the Bearer prefix: A pasted user token travels bare; a token minted by the app's own OAuth grant is refused by the gateway without a Bearer prefix, in the HTTP check and in IDENTIFY alike. The token's kind is now stored with it and applied in one place, so a sign-in that succeeds cannot produce a credential the gateway rejects with 4004.
- The Discord badge is the official mark: The badge in the top right was drawn from the published path through an SVG parser, and the published geometry writes its arc flags with no separators - so the parser lost its place and the mark came out mangled. The geometry is now transcribed command for command with arcToRelative, filled even-odd so the eyes are holes, and rendered from that exact source to check it.
- Two new Home sequel styles: Tickets and Polaroids: Tickets is an admission stub: artwork on one end, a perforated tear-off carrying the close button on the other, with notches cut through the card so they show the page behind. Polaroids is an instant print - a white frame with the title written into its thick bottom margin - lying tilted on the card, each print leaning the same way every time.
- Switching sequel style no longer restarts Home: The chosen style lived in a static CompositionLocal, so picking one rebuilt the whole page and its hero and Continue rail replayed their opening animations at the same moment every row recomposed. The local is dynamic now and the style is read inside each list item, so a switch redraws the sequels and leaves the page above them alone.
- Small engine cleanups: The Discord account mapping existed in three copies and its avatar arithmetic had already drifted between them - it is one function now. The unused path parser import and the duplicated verbatim path constant are gone, and the mark moved into its own file so the glyph catalogue stops growing.
